To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a predictive control scheme is implemented in an indirect matrix converter fed induction machine and that this control scheme is capable of minimizing the reactive power at the input side of this converter.
a predictive torque and flux controlled induction machine fed by indirect matrix converter is proposed.
a predictive torque and flux controller is presented to drive an induction machine fed through a matrix converter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of predictive control in power electronics and electrical machines, and the development of control schemes for the power electronics converters that supply the electrical machines.
the application of predictive control to the control of an indirect matrix converter feeding an induction machine.
the development of a new predictive control scheme for induction machines fed by matrix converters with reactive power minimisation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the predictive control approach can be implemented in an easy way and with a high level of performance.

the proposed predictive torque and flux controller for induction machine drives fed by indirect matrix converter is a simple and efficient approach for the control of the torque, flux and reactive power in induction machine drives fed from indirect matrix converter.

the proposed predictive torque and flux controller for the indirect matrix converter fed induction machine has the following advantages: a) it is simple to be implemented; b) it is very intuitive; c) it has a good torque tracking performance; d) it is able to control the reactive power in the input side with a good performance and e) it has the capability to work in open-loop mode.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose an indirect matrix converter fed by a predictive torque and flux controller with reactive power minimisation strategy, which is able to control the torque and flux with good performance, while at the same time the input currents are with unity power factor.
the predictive approach is a good alternative to control induction machines fed by indirect matrix converters.

we propose a predictive torque and flux controller for an induction machine driven by an indirect matrix-converter, where the control law is based on a one-step prediction horizon, and the control law is very intuitive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed control scheme is very simple and intuitive to be implemented in an actual control system.
the proposed method has the ability to achieve a very good tracking of the references for both the torque and flux and, at the sametime, to achieve a good reactive power minimization.
the predictive control approach is simple to implement and has good performance.
